claims.text: A hybrid Miedema–machine-learning framework will accurately predict melting temperature and entropy of fusion for refractory high-entropy alloys.
CALPHAD predictions for refractory high-entropy alloys fail or become unreliable when assessed binary data are sparse.
The hybrid method is valid when the alloy remains a single-phase BCC solid solution.
NbMoTaW and WNbMoTaV are representative refractory multi-principal-element alloy systems, and WNbMoTaV can form a single BCC phase after vacuum arc melting.
Cast BCC refractory high-entropy alloys can exhibit severe compositional segregation.
Complex binary interactions and large atomic-size differences cause severe segregation or intermetallic formation in standard thermodynamic databases.
The Miedema model has been used to estimate binary-liquid mixing enthalpies and to classify bulk metallic glasses using atomic-size difference and heat of mixing.
Vibrational entropy can be estimated from atomic-size difference and valence-electron concentration using a machine-learning surrogate trained on concentrated-solid-solution thermodynamic data.
For an equimolar alloy with N components, configurational entropy is R ln N, and five or more principal elements produce high configurational entropy.
Experimental melting data and fully assessed binary subsystems are sparse for refractory alloys in the 1000–3000 °C range.
Atomic-size difference, valence-electron concentration, and enthalpy of mixing are established descriptors for phase formation in multicomponent alloys.
Atomic-size difference governs lattice distortion and the magnitude of vibrational entropy.
Miedema mixing enthalpy governs chemical stability and liquidus/solidus boundaries in refractory high-entropy alloys.
The number of binary interactions grows as N(N-1)/2, and the resulting data demand causes unreliable CALPHAD extrapolation for high-melting refractory pairs.
The Miedema model uses macroscopic electronic parameters such as work function and electron density instead of requiring binary phase diagrams.
Vibrational formation entropy is generally about an order of magnitude smaller than configurational entropy in concentrated solid-solution alloys.
The total entropy of fusion can be represented as the sum of configurational and vibrational entropy contributions.
Combining the estimated enthalpy and entropy through the Gibbs free-energy equality permits melting-temperature prediction without a full phase diagram.
The hybrid model will predict melting temperatures within ±5% and outperform standard CALPHAD extrapolations for single-phase BCC NbMoTaW and WNbMoTaV alloys.
A threshold of atomic-size difference above 4% or mixing enthalpy below -15 kJ/mol identifies the onset of dominant intermetallic formation.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis restricts validity to single-phase BCC alloys, whereas the boundary field expands the claimed valid domain to single-phase BCC, FCC, or HCP alloys.
